Issued at 255 PM EDT Fri Oct 2 2026

Through Tonight...Persistent southeast flow coupled with the 
moist air mass in place has produced scattered showers and 
isolated storms across east central Florida this afternoon. 
Continued shower and storm development is forecast over the next 
few hours, with the same storm threats all forecast, including 
occasional to frequent lightning strikes, wind gusts up to 50 mph,
and quick rainfall accumulations of 1-3". Minor, localized 
flooding remains a concern. While coverage is generally 
anticipated to diminish in coverage into the evening and overnight
hours, some hi-res guidance continues isolated activity across 
the peninsula through the overnight hours and into early Saturday,
especially along the coast where onshore- moving showers are 
possible. Flooding will remain a concern through the overnight 
hours, especially in places that have seen rainfall today. 
Temperatures either are peaking or peaked prior to rainfall in the
upper 80s, with conditions tonight remaining muggy with lows in 
the 70s. 

Saturday-Sunday...Mid-level ridging is forecast to remain in 
place across the Florida peninsula this weekend, translating to 
broad high pressure across the western Atlantic at the surface. 
The ridge axis is forecast to remain well north of Florida, 
maintaining east to southeast winds locally. This onshore flow 
will continue to advect moist air towards east central Florida, 
keeping PWATs of 2-2.3" through this weekend. This moist air mass 
coupled with the persistent onshore flow will favor continued 
development of showers across the local Atlantic waters through 
the evening and early morning hours, with coverage increasing and 
expanding towards the peninsula through the late morning and 
afternoon hours. Kept PoPs generally between 30-50% on Saturday, 
increasing to 40-70% on Sunday as moisture continues to advect to 
the area. Isolated to scattered storm development will be possible
each day, though the moist profile and limited forcing will keep 
chances limited. Occasional lightning strikes, wind gusts up to 45
mph, and quick rainfall accumulations of 1-3" will be possible 
each day. Minor, localized flooding in spots cannot be ruled out, 
especially given saturated soils from recent rainfall. Storm 
chances will wane into the overnight hours with lingering shower 
chances across the local Atlantic waters. 

The warm, moist air mass will support temperatures remaining near
to slightly above normal, with highs climbing into the mid 80s to
low 90s. These temperatures combined with humidity will produce 
peak heat indices of 100F and greater through the weekend, so 
adequate hydration and breaks in the shade are strongly encouraged
if spending extended periods of time outdoors. Overnight, 
temperatures will range between the low to mid 70s.

Monday-Thursday...Mid-level ridging across the eastern US will 
weaken into early next week as broad troughing builds and extends 
across the southeastern US. This troughing aloft will support a 
cold front drifting southward across the southeast US, with the 
front anticipated to stall near to just north of Florida through 
next week. The development of a low along the stalled boundary 
directly near the northeastern Florida coast looks to be possible 
on Tuesday based on guidance, with the low then lifting 
northeastward across the Atlantic waters. This overall set-up will
maintain a deep pocket of moisture across the Florida peninsula, 
with PoPs forecast to remain high (70-90%) through next week. 
Heavy rainfall will be the primary concern with activity and WPC 
is already beginning to include northern portions of east central 
Florida under Marginal risks (1/4) of excessive rainfall on Monday
and Tuesday. Minor, localized flooding in spots will be possible,
especially given the saturated soils from recent rainfall. Storm 
development will also be possible with activity, and lightning and
gusty winds cannot be ruled out. Greater ideas on exact rainfall 
chances and storm hazards will become clearer as time moves on. 
Temperatures are forecast to remain near to slightly above normal 
on Monday in the upper 80s to low 90s, with a chance for peak heat
indices to once again reach 100F in spots. A temperature gradient
from north to south is forecast Tuesday through Thursday due to 
the stationary boundary, with afternoon highs remaining a bit 
closer to normal. Overnight lows will remain close to normal 
through the period.
